summary: Lin Heng is an Indologist who studied at Silpakorn University, where he earned an MA under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).
Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
Linda Learman specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She pursued doctoral research under Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral work under Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1993. She served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. McCune completed an MA supervised by Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2007) and studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark is a scholar in Sinology who has served as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji specializes in Sinology. Ji earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the doctoral supervision of Chi Xiao and Yuet Keung Lo (attested 2014).

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1966–1972), later holding a post at the University of Tartu (~1969–2010).

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist educated at the University of Liverpool and Trinity College, Cambridge. He worked as Keeper at the British Museum and held appointments at University College London and SOAS University of London.

Lionel Obadia (b. 1969) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He has held academic posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) was a Tibetology scholar. He held positions at West China Union University (~1946–1950), the State Council of the People's Republic of China (~1950–1959), and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1959–1978).

Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She has held posts at Stanford University (attested 1996) and as an assistant professor (助教授) at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA from the University of Oslo (attested 2008). Peipina studied under MA supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003 and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Liu Zaifu (1941–2026) was a Sinology and philosophy scholar who studied at Xiamen University. He directed the CASS Institute of Literature and lectured at Chicago, Stockholm, Colorado, City University of Hong Kong, and HKUST.

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and the University of Munich, where he earned his Dr.phil. (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery (~1945–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. He founded and headed the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Drubwang Shakya Shri, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Lobsang Shastri is a scholar of Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).
